{{Short description|German mathematician}}
'''Heinz-Otto Kreiss''' (14 September 1930 – 16 December 2015) was a German [[mathematician]] in the fields of [[numerical analysis]], [[applied mathematics]], and what was the new area of [[computing]] in the early 1960s. Born in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]], he earned his Ph.D. at [[Kungliga Tekniska Högskolan]] in 1959. Over the course of his long career, Kreiss wrote a number of books in addition to the purely academic journal articles he authored across several disciplines. He was professor at [[Uppsala University]], [[California Institute of Technology]] and [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). He was also a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]. At the time of his death, Kreiss was a [[Sweden|Swedish]] citizen, living in [[Stockholm]]. He died in Stockholm in 2015, aged 85.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/news/memoriam-heinz-otto-kreiss | title=In Memoriam: Heinz-Otto Kreiss | publisher=[[UCLA]] Department of Mathematics | date=18 December 2015 | accessdate=20 December 2015}}</ref>
 
Kreiss did research on the initial value problem for partial differential equations, numerical treatment of partial differential equations, difference equations, and applications to hydrodynamics and meteorology.

In 1974, he delivered a plenary lecture ''Initial Boundary Value Problems for Hyperbolic Partial Differential Equations'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in [[Vancouver]]. In 2002 he won the [[National Academy of Sciences]] Award in Numerical Analysis and Applied Mathematics.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20111119222343/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/nas-award-in-applied.html NAS Award in Applied Mathematics and Numerical Analysis]</ref> In 2003 he was the [[John von Neumann Lecture|John von Neumann Lecturer]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM). He was elected a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

His doctoral students include [[Björn Engquist]] and [[Bertil Gustafsson]]. His daughter, [[Gunilla Kreiss]], was a student of Engquist.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=12003}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* with Jens Lorenz: Initial-boundary value problems and the Navier-Stokes equations, Academic Press 1989, SIAM 2004<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Initial-boundary value problems and the Navier-Stokes equations'' by Heinz-Otto Kreiss and Jens Lorenz|author=Constantin, Peter|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|volume=23|year=1990|pages=555–559|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1990-15979-8|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* with Hedwig Ulmer Busenhart: Time-dependent partial differential equations and their numerical solution, Birkhäuser 2001
* with [[Bertil Gustafsson]], [[Joseph Oliger]]: time-dependent problems and difference methods, Wiley 1995
